proof:
The sections converge in Hausdorff distance to either endpoint section: interpolation of that section with a fixed interior point gives the lower inclusion, and compactness gives the upper inclusion. Volume is continuous under this convergence. For $d\ge1$, Brunn–Minkowski gives a nonnegative concave function $f^{1/d}$ on $[a,b]$. A continuous concave function on a compact interval is absolutely continuous: its monotone one-sided derivatives integrate to its increments in the interior and the endpoint increments follow by monotone convergence on the two monotonicity intervals. Composition with the Lipschitz power map on its bounded range gives absolute continuity of $f$. For $d=0$ the function is constant on the interval. Thus $Df=f'\mathbf 1_{(a,b)}dt+f(a)\delta_a-f(b)\delta_b$.

Integrate $Bf'$ by parts on the pieces cut by the interior integers. Each interior jump contributes $f(k)$ and the smooth derivative contributes $-\int f$. The remaining endpoint terms are $B(b-)f(b)-B(a+)f(a)$. Adding the atoms of $Df$ cancels the noninteger endpoint terms. At an integer endpoint the atom has coefficient zero and the one-sided term contributes half its fiber value, yielding the displayed correction for the closed sum.

For a smooth test $g$, the divergence theorem for the vector field $(g(z),0)$ gives $\int_{\partial A}g(z)N_z\,d\mathcal H_d=\int g'(z)f(z)\,dz=-\int g\,dDf$. Smooth $B$ with even approximate identities and use a cutoff outside the relevant projection. The smoothed values converge pointwise to the stated representative, including zero at the integers, and are uniformly bounded. Dominated convergence for both finite measures gives the flux formula. Finally, if a lower-dimensional convex set has a positive-volume vertical $d$-slice, that slice spans its entire affine hull, which is the same vertical hyperplane. Otherwise every slice has zero $d$-volume.
statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with projection $[a,b]$ and put $f(t)=|A_t|_d$ on this interval and zero outside. For $d=0$ use $f=1$ on $[a,b]$. Define $B(t)=t-\lfloor t\rfloor-1/2$ off the integers and zero on them, and let $Df$ be the distributional derivative of the zero extension. The closed-fiber sum satisfies
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}f(k)=\int f(t)\,dt+\int B\,dDf
+\tfrac12\big(\mathbf 1_{a\in\mathbb Z} f(a)+\mathbf 1_{b\in\mathbb Z}f(b)\big).
$$
For polytopes $\int B\,dDf=-\int_{\partial A}B(z)N_z\,d\mathcal H_d$, where $N_z$ is the base component of the outward unit normal. A lower-dimensional compact convex set can have positive mixed $d$-volume only if it lies in one plane $z=a$ with $a\in\mathbb Z$, in which case its mixed volume is $|A_a|_d$.
title: Exact one-coordinate sampling flux with closed endpoint correction
